transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy. But I know they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts, trying to keep me from getting the supervisor spot.
About how long has this been going on?
About ten months now—since I started trying to get the shift-supervisor position and the arguments got worse.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
Sometimes, yeah. At work in an aisle, or when I’m folding clothes at home, I hear a man’s voice really clearly say, “Nicole, check it again,” even though nobody’s around.
During these past ten months, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or hopeless?
I’m not really sure what you mean by persistently. I’ve been stressed and upset about what’s been happening, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt hopeless.
Have you had times where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
Yeah. There’ve been weeks when I only sleep maybe three hours, wake up before my alarm, and still feel like I don’t need any more rest to get going.
Do the experiences of hearing voices or feeling watched also happen during times when your sleep and energy are completely normal?

Yeah. There were a few quieter weeks where I was sleeping more normally and wasn’t rushing around so much, but I still heard the voice telling me to check things. I still felt like the pallet counts were being changed against me, too.
